message.abstract: <jats:p>Institutional analysis can help explain how people coordinate collective work but its diverse evidence base often spans constitutional documents, formal procedures, technical records, informal expectations, and recorded public debate. I examine how artificial intelligence (AI) agents can use Institutional Grammar 2.0 to reconstruct institutional relationships and support governance analysis. Bitcoin Core provides a demanding case because authority over software development intersects with participants' aspirations and choices in a decentralized monetary network. The study combines 12 routine development episodes with six linked proposals from the Core-Knots dispute. Eighteen independent AI agent coding runs compare two instruction specifications, followed by collaborative agent review of interpretive differences. The analysis identifies locally recognized expectations, distinguishes control over different decisions, and connects software implementation choices to disagreements about authority and Bitcoin's purpose. Independent coding revealed interpretive differences, and the more detailed specification did not improve overall agreement. Collaborative review corrected coding errors, narrowed disagreements, and clarified case conclusions while retaining defensible alternative interpretations. The findings support a method for organizing dispersed institutional evidence into relationships that analysts can inspect and identifying governance questions that require human judgment. The study provides a foundation for extending AI-assisted institutional analysis across complex public records, with humans directing research priorities, assessing consequential interpretations, and choosing among competing values.</jats:p>
title: AI-assisted institutional analysis of a decentralized protocol: applying Institutional Grammar 2.0 to Bitcoin Core
